question.text: NAV (Net Asset Value) of a mutual fund is best defined as:

answer.text: Total AUM minus expenses divided by units
(Market value of portfolio securities plus income, minus liabilities, costs and expenses) divided by outstanding units
The prevailing market price of the scheme's units

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines NAV as net assets divided by the number of units outstanding, where net assets are arrived at by taking the current mark-to-market value of the portfolio plus income, and deducting liabilities, costs and expenses. This is the explicit per-unit value formula. The Trap: "Total assets / units" and "AUM minus expenses / units" both omit important deductions (liabilities or income inclusions) and so understate the rigour of the NAV calculation. Market price refers to traded price (relevant for ETFs), not the accounting NAV. Note: NAV is calculated each business day; for purchase and redemption requests, the applicable NAV is determined as per the scheme's stated cut-off rules.
